question: Does the pooled flipper-length predictor have lower mean absolute error than a training-median constant on the original 2009 holdout?
review_trigger: original/research/review.md, Interpretation and verification: 'A median would minimize training absolute error among constant predictors, so the result compares the line specifically with the **training mean**.' This is a limitation, not a reported error in the original estimates.
timing: Supplement specified before this median rerun only. The original fit, scores, cohort and reviewer concern were already public and inspected. This is reuse of the same holdout, not a new independent confirmation. No median holdout score has been calculated for this supplement before freezing.
protocol: Use original/data/penguins.csv from palmerpenguins v0.1.0. Keep rows with measured flipper length and body mass, independent of other missing fields; identify rows by one-based CSV data row. Fit all predictors on the same 2007 and 2008 rows. Predict each eligible 2009 row once with the training mean mass, training median mass (average middle pair if even), and pooled least-squares line with intercept from flipper length alone. No imputation, stratification, tuning, new split or test-mass use in fitting.
evaluation: Unweighted mean absolute error (MAE, g) over identical test rows. Report all three scores, the training median constant, and the signed mean-minus-line and median-minus-line MAE differences calculated before rounding. A positive difference favors the line; report zero or negative without changing models. Compare row IDs, original measurements, original predictions, original MAEs and mean-minus-line difference to the archived tables at their stored nine decimal places. Replay must match outputs byte for byte. Display errors to three decimal places (0.0005 g tolerance).
scope: Deterministic descriptive errors for the observed eligible records, not a sampling distribution. No confidence interval or claim about other years, populations, within-species associations or causality. One CPU, Python standard library, one formal comparison and one reproduction; stop regardless of sign.

criteria.description: Report the common training and test counts.
Identify the added constant and report all three common-cohort errors.
Report both signed baseline-minus-linear MAE differences; compare with the earlier manuscript and limit the conclusion to this holdout.
